reasoning_content:
Interesting — this time the same pattern worked. The Podman errors were probably transient — likely process-compose, when I sent TERM to pid 18011, started shutting down and its cleanup handler (which includes container integration) ran and printed to stderr, and that coincided with my command. Actually, more likely: when I killed the process-compose process, its shutdown ran the "container integration" cleanup (podman), and that stderr output got mixed in. No, that's not it either... the error appeared in the output of my command that ran before the kill was issued...

Wait, actually the first time (curl -X POST /project/stop), the response body itself was the podman error — because process-compose's /project/stop endpoint tries to stop associated containers via podman if it's configured. It's possible the project config in process-compose.yaml includes a container. Let me check whether process-compose.yaml has a containers section.

In any case, the podman errors on the two subsequent commands were strange. The environment probably has a wrapper. Let me now properly check the state: is process-compose still alive (yes, pids 17988/18011 still show up), and are the app processes running?

action.command:
grep -n "containers" /workspace/process-compose.yaml | head; echo "---"; ps -eo pid,etimes,args --no-headers | grep -E "uvicorn src.main|python main.py|vite|db_pipelines" | grep -v grep | wc -l; /workspace/.venv/bin/python -c "
res=set()
for f in ('/proc/net/tcp','/proc/net/tcp6'):
    try: lines=open(f).read().splitlines()[1:]
    except FileNotFoundError: continue
    for ln in lines:
        p=ln.split()
        if p[3]=='0A': res.add(int(p[1].split(':')[1],16))
want=[18000,18001,18002,18003,18005,18006,18007,18008,18009,18010,18011,18012,18013,18014,18015,18016,18020,18021,18022,18024,3002,8080]
print('listening:', sorted([p for p in want if p in res]))
"
